topics.name: Listening and Speaking
subtopics: Teacher chooses two themes for weeks 1-5 and two new themes for weeks 6-10 to introduce and recycle vocabulary and language structures

Daily oral activities using a theme such as 'Wild Animals': follows and gives instructions; answers 'When/Why/Where/How' questions; asks for clarification; makes requests; short conversations on familiar topics
Identifies an object from a simple oral description ('I am a very big animal... Who am I?'); talks about objects in a picture or photograph
Listens to a simple recount and, with help, gives one; uses the past tense in context ('I saw a giraffe')
Memorises and performs poems, action rhymes and songs; plays language games ('Guess who I am')

Focused listening (twice a week): listens to stories (e.g. How the Giraffe got its Long Neck) and recounts; answers comprehension questions; predicts what happens next; expresses feelings about the story; retells it
Listens to a non-fiction text (factual recount or information report, e.g. on elephants), answers questions and, with help, gives a simple summary
Builds conceptual vocabulary (animals: appearance, habitat); countable and uncountable nouns, articles 'a' and 'the', simple present and past tense in speech
Informal assessment weeks 1-5: responds to 'When/Why' questions; identifies an object from an oral description; weeks 6-10: retells a story orally; participates in a conversation on a familiar topic

topics.name: Phonics
subtopics: Identifies letter-sound relationships of all single letters, noting Home vs Additional Language pronunciation differences
Recognises consonant digraphs sh, ch, th, wh at the beginning of words (sh-ip, ch-ip, th-in, wh-en)
Distinguishes different vowel sounds aurally (the 'u' in put and in bus)
Builds and sounds out 3- and 4-letter words using sounds learnt

topics.name: Phonics
subtopics: Recognises consonant digraphs sh, ch, th at the end of words (fi-sh, ri-ch, wi-th)
Recognises vowel digraphs ('oo' in boot, 'oa' in boat)
Builds and sounds out 3- and 4-letter words using sounds learnt

topics.name: Reading
subtopics: Shared Reading (within Listening and Speaking time): reads a short Big Book or enlarged text with the teacher, using the title to predict; answers literal questions; describes how the story made them feel (code-switching if necessary)

Group Guided Reading (45-75 minutes a week): 5 same-ability groups with graded readers at instructional level (90-95% word accuracy), one group a day for 15 minutes, or whole-class guided reading 3 times a week at minimum time

Reads aloud from own book with the group; uses Home Language reading strategies (phonics, context clues, structural analysis, sight words) to make sense and self-monitor; reads with fluency, expression and attention to punctuation; builds sight vocabulary

Independent reading: reads own and others' writing, Guided Reading books, caption and picture story books from the reading corner, familiar poems and rhymes; uses picture dictionaries for unknown words

topics.name: Writing
subtopics: Uses handwriting skills taught in Home Language
Writes increasingly complex lists with headings (e.g. Wild Animals: elephants, giraffes, lions)
Writes a simple text such as a birthday card
With guidance, writes a simple set of instructions (e.g. a recipe)
Writes a paragraph of 4-6 sentences on a familiar topic

Uses the writing process; punctuation taught in Home Language (. , ? ! and inverted commas); spells common words and attempts unfamiliar words using phonics; builds a word bank and personal dictionary; uses children's dictionaries

topics.name: Language Use
subtopics: Understands and uses the simple present tense
Understands and uses 'There is / There are' (There is a book on the table)
Understands and uses the possessive form of nouns (the book's cover)
Revises grammar covered informally in Grades R-2

sba: Formal Assessment Activity 1 - Listening and speaking: listens to a non-fiction text and answers questions orally; gives a 3-4 sentence oral summary; shows vocabulary by pointing to objects on instruction
Formal Assessment Activity 1 - Phonics: letter-sound relationships of all single letters; consonant digraphs sh, ch, th, wh at the beginning and sh, ch, th at the end of words
Formal Assessment Activity 1 - Reading: retells a story or summarises a non-fiction text (Shared Reading); reads at own level in a guided group using sight words, phonics and comprehension skills
Formal Assessment Activity 1 - Writing: writes a paragraph of 4-6 sentences on a familiar topic; Language use: writes meaningful sentences in the simple present tense
notes: No Grade 3 English FAL ATP is published on the DBE Foundation Phase ATP page; this term is built from the CAPS Grades 1-3 English FAL document (Grade 3 requirements per term), which splits some strands into weeks 1-5 and 6-10 but gives no weekly plan or themes
